artifacts.title: Drupalgeddon2 RCE to snap install privesc (Armageddon)
artifacts.starting_access: unauthenticated web access to Drupal 7 on port 80
artifacts.outcome: root via malicious snap install hook
transferable_properties: check CHANGELOG.txt on Drupal sites for the exact version
read settings.php for database credentials when you have file read
database credentials often reused as system passwords
adapt to blocked outbound with file read and DB queries instead of reverse shells
sudo snap install with wildcard is a direct privesc via root hooks
on CentOS/RHEL the sudoers group is wheel

hypotheses.statement: Drupal 7.56 is vulnerable to Drupalgeddon2 RCE

selected_action.intent: confirm the Drupal version and map the CMS

evidence.summary: confirmed Drupal 7.56 via CHANGELOG.txt, vulnerable to CVE-2018-7600

hypotheses.statement: RCE lets us read files and query the DB to extract credentials

selected_action.intent: run the Drupalgeddon2 exploit and read settings.php + query MySQL

evidence.summary: got RCE as apache, read DB credentials from settings.php, extracted and cracked the Drupal hash, then logged in over SSH as brucetherealadmin

observations: sudo -l allows snap install as root NOPASSWD

hypotheses.statement: a malicious snap with an install hook runs as root

selected_action.intent: build a malicious snap that adds a sudoer user and install it

evidence.summary: packaged a snap with a root install hook that created the pwned sudoer, installed with sudo snap install --dangerous --devmode, then SSHed as pwned and sudo su to root
